name: Tinted amber glass slab desk
objectClass: desk / writing table (glass slab construction); class range 1.00–1.80 m wide, 0.55–0.80 m deep, 0.70–0.76 m high

reasons: Single view only; the back long edge, the rear face of both end panels and the whole underside of the top slab are unseen and must be mirrored/inferred.

Object is a transmissive tinted glass assembly — the read colour is partly transmission plus the backdrop behind it, so albedo values are an estimate with the lighting and see-through stacking removed.
The bronze L-brackets are small and partly blurred: their plate outline is readable but fastener count and bracket depth must be approximated procedurally.
Macro silhouette is unambiguous and bilaterally symmetric, so the hidden half is safely inferable.

notes: Observation: three glass planes only — one horizontal slab and two vertical end panels — with no apron, stretcher, drawer or leg visible. Inference: the structure is bracket-fixed glass-to-glass with no frame.
Silhouette: an open ∏ (inverted U) when viewed along the long axis; bounding volume 1.40 m (X) × 0.72 m (Y) × 0.65 m (Z). Footprint is two thin rectangles 0.60 m × 0.015 m, ≈1.30 m apart on centres.
Proportions against the 1.40 m top width as reference: height 0.51×, depth 0.46×, end-panel height 0.49×, end-panel depth 0.43×, glass thickness 0.011×, top overhang past each panel 0.025×.
Macro parts (3): (1) top slab, (2) −X end panel, (3) +X end panel.
Meso parts: four L-brackets (one at each of the four inner top corners), four polished slab edges, eight polished panel edges, four floor pads.
Micro parts: bracket fastener clusters (inferred 2 screws into panel, 2 into slab underside per bracket), edge arrises on all glass, contact shadow seams at panel-to-slab junctions.

Spatial relationships: the top slab RESTS ON the top edges of both end panels, face-to-edge, with the slab underside flush to each panel's 0.015 m top edge; each panel's outer face sits ≈0.035 m inboard of the slab's end edge. Each L-bracket is BOLTED to the inner face of an end panel on one leg and to the underside of the slab on the other leg, its outer arris FLUSH with the panel's top edge. Panels are set back ≈0.025 m from the slab's front and back long edges. Floor pads are ADHERED to the bottom edge of each panel and CONTACT the floor.

Colour and finish by region: top face — amber-orange hue ≈25°, mid-high value, medium-high saturation, gloss; end panels — same hue, value falling with height; brackets — near-neutral dark brown, satin metallic.

Gradient on each end panel outer face, ordered stops bottom→top along the 0.70 m height: 0.00 #6E3312, 0.20 #8F4517, 0.55 #A85824, 0.85 #A0521F, 1.00 #98501F. Treat as transmission density variation, not paint.
Hidden: the entire back long edge of the desk, the rear faces of both end panels, the underside of the top slab, and the interior/knee space beyond what the near panel occludes.
Assumed left-right symmetry: the +X end panel and its bracket pair are mirrored from the visible −X assembly; the photo shows no evidence against this.
Assumed front-back symmetry of the bracket layout: two brackets per panel, front and back, with the rear pair inferred from the partially visible rear fittings.

Uncertain: exact glass thickness (read as 0.012–0.018 m from the slab edge band), bracket leg length (±0.03 m), and whether the tint is body-tinted glass or a laminated interlayer — inference favours body tint because the edge band is the same hue, only darker.
Uncertain: floor pads are visible only on the near panel; mirrored onto the far panel by inference.
Background is a plain warm-grey studio sweep with a soft contact shadow only beneath the near panel, which weakens the camera-height estimate.
